title: Extending an admissible blowup from an open algebraic subspace
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Open and closed immersions mean representable morphisms whose scheme base changes have the indicated property [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], write $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T$ for the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$, constructed by etale descent of the ordinary scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] on affine etale charts. Finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections. Let $T$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and let $U,V\subseteq T$ be quasi-compact open subspaces. Let $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_V$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal with $\mathcal J|_{U\cap V}=\mathcal O_{U\cap V}$. There exists a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ with $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$ and an isomorphism over $V$ $$\bigl(\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}T\bigr)\times_TV\ \cong\ \operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}V.$$ Under the canonical blowup identifications over $U\cap V$, this isomorphism restricts to the identity. In particular the latter blowup is an open subspace of the former. No inclusion between $U$ and $V$ is assumed.

proof.text:
Put $W=U\cup V$. The disjoint union of quasi-compact etale scheme atlases of $U$ and $V$ is a quasi-compact etale scheme atlas of $W$, so $W$ is quasi-compact. Define an ideal subsheaf $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_W$ by
$$\mathcal K(E)=\{s\in\mathcal O_W(E):s|_{E\times_WV}\in\mathcal J(E\times_WV)\}$$
for each etale scheme $E\to W$. This is a sheaf of ideals: restrictions preserve the condition, and local sections satisfying it glue in $\mathcal O_W$ and satisfy it by the sheaf axiom for $\mathcal J$. It restricts to $\mathcal J$ on $V$ and to $\mathcal O_U$ on $U$, since $\mathcal J$ is the unit ideal on $U\cap V$. These equalities give finite local generators on the cover $W=U\cup V$ (the generator $1$ on $U$, and those of $\mathcal J$ on $V$). They also give local presentations of $\mathcal K$: the given presentations of $\mathcal J$ on $V$ and the presentation $0\to\mathcal O_U\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_U\to0$ on $U$. Thus $\mathcal K$ is quasi-coherent by [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. This is direct sheaf gluing, requiring no affineness of the intersection.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-submodule-extension] with $X=T$, open $W=U\cup V$, ambient module $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_T$, and submodule $\mathcal G=\mathcal K$. The ambient structure module is quasi-coherent, with its one-generator identity presentation; $T$ is qcqs by hypothesis, and $W$ is quasi-compact by step 1. We obtain a finite-type quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ whose restriction to $W$ is $\mathcal K$. An $\mathcal O_T$-submodule of $\mathcal O_T$ is an ideal, since closure under multiplication by local ring sections is exactly scalar closure. Consequently $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$ and $\mathcal I|_V=\mathcal J$, as ideal subsheaves, not just as abstract modules.

source.place: Tag 086D (lemma-extend-admissible-blowups), proof: application of Limits of Spaces Tag 0853 (lemma-extend).

proof.text: Form $T'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}T$. The open-restriction clause of [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties] identifies $T'\times_TV$ canonically over $V$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I|_V}V=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}V$. It applies to the finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ on an algebraic space, and explicitly covers open immersions, so no additional flatness hypothesis is needed here. This proves the required isomorphism.

On $U$, the ideal $\mathcal I$ is the unit ideal, so $U$ lies in the complement of its zero subspace. By the complement-isomorphism clause of [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties], $T'\times_TU\to U$ is an isomorphism; the same clause applied to $\mathcal J$ identifies its blowup over $U\cap V$ with $U\cap V$. The isomorphism of step 3 is over $V$, hence over $U\cap V$ after restriction. After these identifications it is an endomorphism of $U\cap V$ over itself, necessarily its identity. Finally $T'\times_TV$ is the inverse-image open subspace of $T'$; composing its open inclusion with the inverse of the step-3 isomorphism exhibits $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}V$ as an open subspace of $T'$.
